title: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild
abstract: arXiv:2611.25215v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings. ROAM combines the world knowledge of a Vision-Language Model (VLM), pre-trained on internet-scale data, with robust locomotion and local planning policies learned in simulation via reinforcement learning (RL). The VLM provides common-sense reasoning and semantic interpretation of the scene, assessing risks, interpreting signs, and producing semantic labels with associated navigation costs. translated_title: 桥接视觉-语言推理与学习控制以实现野外足式机器人导航
translated_abstract: 在多样化真实环境中的自主导航仍然是机器人领域最大的挑战之一，它既需要鲁棒的底层运动控制来应对复杂地形，又需要高层推理能力来解读环境线索。我们提出了ROAM（Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility，鲁棒开放世界自主移动）系统，该系统能够使足式机器人在复杂的高山和城市场景中完成公里级导航。ROAM将基于互联网规模数据预训练的视觉-语言模型（VLM）所具备的世界知识，与通过强化学习（RL）在仿真中学习到的鲁棒运动控制和局部规划策略相结合。VLM提供常识推理和场景语义解读，能够评估风险、解读标识牌，并生成带有相应导航代价的语义标签。一个开放词汇分割模块将这些标签转换为稠密的实时风险地图，用以调节两个预训练的强化学习策略。
tldr: 该论文提出ROAM系统，将视觉-语言模型的常识推理能力与强化学习习得的运动控制和局部规划策略相结合，使足式机器人能够在高山和城市等复杂真实环境中实现公里级自主导航。
en_tdlr: This paper presents ROAM, a system that bridges vision-language model reasoning with RL-learned locomotion and local planning policies, enabling legged robots to autonomously navigate kilometer-scale routes in challenging real-world alpine and urban environments.
